rows.selection_reason: No experiments are completed yet, so the main uncertainty is the baseline performance of a simple, low-confounding model. config_001 tests a minimal RNA-only, single-profile PCA baseline with no aggregation or fusion, establishing a reference for RNA representation quality and for later comparisons to multiprofile, learned RNA encoders, image-only, and multimodal settings. It is the best first use of budget because it is simple, interpretable, and isolates the core RNA signal before adding complexity.

The only completed run is a single-profile RNA PCA baseline, so there is no evidence yet about whether image features are useful or how they compare to RNA. config_010 tests image-only performance with a simple single-profile ResNet50 baseline, keeping profile setting minimal and avoiding fusion/aggregation changes. This is the best next experiment because it reduces uncertainty about the modality choice before investing in multimodal fusion or more complex profile settings, and it provides a direct baseline for later multimodal ResNet50 comparisons.

The only strong result so far is RNA-only PCA single-profile (0.485 accuracy), while image-only ResNet is weak (0.208 accuracy), leaving uncertainty about whether a learned RNA representation can improve the best modality. config_004 keeps the model setting and single-profile setting fixed and changes only the RNA encoder from PCA to scvi_n200, cleanly isolating the representation effect. This is the best next experiment because it directly compares against the current best RNA baseline before adding more complex choices such as multiprofile aggregation or fusion, and its result will guide whether to invest in scvi-based RNA or multimodal variants.

RNA-only scvi_n200 singleprofile is the current best configuration (accuracy 0.520, F1 0.498), while image-only ResNet50 is much weaker, so the most promising direction is RNA representation. The key untested design choice is whether multiprofile aggregation improves performance. config_005 extends the best RNA encoder to multiprofile using the simplest aggregation, avgpool, avoiding unnecessary changes to fusion or transformer aggregation. Compared with config_004, it clarifies the effect of multiprofile for the strongest RNA encoder and sets up a clean follow-up comparison with transformer aggregation.

The strongest completed result is config_005, RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and avgpool, reaching 0.650 accuracy and 0.628 F1, while image-only resnet50 is weak and multimodal settings would introduce multiple new factors. config_006 tests the same RNA encoder and multiprofile setting but replaces avgpool with transformer aggregation, directly isolating the effect of aggregation in the currently most promising design. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest evidence, may improve validation accuracy, and clarifies whether a more expressive aggregation is worthwhile before adding image or fusion complexity.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile RNA modeling with scvi_n200 substantially outperforms singleprofile RNA models, and transformer aggregation is slightly better than avgpool for scvi_n200. The key uncertainty is whether this multiprofile gain is specific to scvi_n200 or also applies to simpler PCA representations. config_003 tests pca_n2000 under the same multiprofile + transformer setting as the current best RNA-only model, directly isolating the effect of RNA representation while also clarifying whether multiprofile helps PCA. This is a high-value, low-complexity next step because it avoids introducing image modality or fusion before the RNA-side design choices are better understood.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200, especially with transformer aggregation, reaching about 0.653 validation accuracy. In contrast, image evidence is sparse and weak: image-only ResNet50 single-profile performs poorly at about 0.208 accuracy. config_013 tests whether a stronger ImageNet ViT-L image encoder can make the image modality useful in the simplest image-only setting, isolating image representation from RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion choices. This is the best next experiment because it reduces the key uncertainty of whether image features are worth using before investing in more complex multimodal configurations, while still potentially identifying a strong image-only baseline.

The strongest evidence is RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200, especially config_006 (accuracy 0.6530, F1 0.6283), while image-only models are weak (about 0.21-0.23 accuracy). The main remaining uncertainty is whether adding image information to the strong RNA representation can improve performance. config_038 extends the best RNA-only setting by adding the better image-only encoder, imagenet_vit_l, with concat fusion while keeping the same multiprofile and transformer aggregation. This is the best next experiment because it directly tests the multimodal/fusion question with minimal unnecessary changes, and it will clarify whether further investment in multimodal variants is worthwhile.

The strongest evidence so far is that scvi_n200 with multiprofile RNA aggregation is much better than PCA, and the only multimodal test, config_038 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat), is the best configuration at 0.7207 accuracy and 0.6815 F1. However, the fusion rule is still uncertain because only concat has been tested in this promising multimodal setting. config_039 changes only concat to weighted, isolating the effect of fusion while preserving the current best architecture. This is the best next experiment because it directly exploits the strongest observed direction, tests an important untested design decision, and will clarify whether weighted fusion can improve the best configuration or whether concat should be retained.

The strongest evidence is that the best completed model is multimodal multiprofile scVI + ViT + transformer + weighted (config_039, 0.725), and RNA encoder choice has already shown a large effect, with PCA much weaker than scVI in comparable multiprofile settings. scGPT remains untested, so the key uncertainty is whether it can match or improve the scVI RNA representation in the current best multimodal architecture. This experiment changes only the RNA encoder from scVI to scGPT while holding the image encoder, profile setting, aggregation, and fusion fixed, directly isolating the RNA representation effect. It is the best next use of budget because it extends the most promising direction with a single-factor comparison and can either produce a new best configuration or efficiently rule out scGPT before further exploration.
